Objects and identities

Data model

Object chain

Object Producer and input Required interpretation
Campaign record Supplied JSON descriptor Tune order, runtime, source factorization, seed and block rules
Raw ROOT PYTHIA producer Event vectors, scalar diagnostics and generator metadata
Analyzed shard analyze run from accepted raw sources Typed event and particle rows plus embedded contract and PASS receipt
Query workspace query build from an analyzed pair Exact support rows, sparse histograms, dictionary and manifest
Sharded collection Collector or collection create One checked locator across exact global source membership
Merged collection merge build Sparse partitions by tune and block, with original support-file references
Numerical package reduce run Typed ROOT values, covariance, missing states, provenance and exports
Figure directory plot render-cold PDFs, ROOT canvases, drawing record and exact manifest
Collaboration package package build Required numerical and figure files with relative locators

Source and event identities

A natural source key contains tune and logical job ID. An accepted attempt supplies its attempt ID and seed. Global source IDs enumerate the canonical manifest order. source_id columns inside individual ROOT shards remain local. Receipt mappings connect local IDs to the global domain.

The event identifier uses a 64-bit unsigned integer. Its fields contain 16 campaign bits, 2 tune bits, 14 logical-job bits, 12 attempt bits and 20 successful-event bits. The event index identifies successful events within the source. It is not a generator trial count.

The raw manifest stores one canonical JSON object per line. Its fields are tune, logical_id, accepted_attempt, accepted_seed, block, successful_events, bytes, raw_sha256, raw_storage_key, validation_log_sha256 and validation_receipt_sha256. The validator requires exact membership, ordering and coherent seed/block identities.

The attempt CSV stores tune, logical_id, attempt, seed, outcome, evidence_status and raw_storage_key. Its join with accepted sources distinguishes job outcomes from generator event trials. The campaign also pins the evidence inventory and accepted producer identity.

Raw and analyzed ROOT

Raw ROOT uses schema hf_primary_ground_raw_v7. The event tree contains heavy-particle vectors, ancestry, selected hard roots, activity and generator diagnostics. Additional objects record settings, particle stability, process counts, weights and source metadata. validate_raw.cpp defines required branches and cross-checks.

The analyzer writes the following tables:

Table Meaning
events Event ID, weight, both activity counts, process code, pTHat, hard scale and MPI count
heavy Signed species, status, flags, heavy valence and particle four-vectors
hard Selected hard-process roots
ancestry, ancestry_mothers, heavy_mothers Complete retained mother relationships and ancestry identities
origins, constituents Resolved or unresolved origin decisions for hadrons and heavy constituents
triggers Structural trigger candidates and rejection masks
pairs Ordered trigger–associate pairs, signs, kinematics and origin categories
closure Full and visible heavy-flavour closure terms
event_compatibility Event-level compatibility diagnostics
event_ranges Contiguous source event-ID ranges
sources, source_blocks, source_counts Local source identities, original blocks, event exposure and table counts

The embedded contract object binds schemas, registries, metadata and scientific row digests. The adjacent JSON receipt binds physical ROOT SHA-256 and size to source and execution records. Verification checks natural keys, foreign keys, row order and scientific semantics.

The analyzer preserves the retained raw information, not the complete PYTHIA event record. It uses ZSTD level 5, bounded baskets and periodic event flushing. Its schema digest fixes branch names, types and order.

Query workspace

A complete workspace has exactly these seven files:

File Contract
query.root Support TTrees, five THnSparseD objects, query_spec and metadata
query.tsv Exact construction specification for the native query executable
analysis.json Construction-time downstream model
layout.json Exact query schema
dictionary.json Campaign-wide signed-PDG census and digest
metadata.json Input receipt, identities, retained rows, sparse facts and pair-population proof
manifest.json Exact file hashes, sizes and scientific-content identity

A dictionary ordinal is meaningful only with its dictionary digest. Every query shard in a collection must use the same dictionary body. The builder refuses observed PDGs outside that dictionary.

Sparse contents use weighted additive counts. Sumw2 stores squared-weight accumulation. These stored sums do not replace the block jackknife covariance of nonlinear observables. The query retains both activity definitions simultaneously and has no sparse replica for each pT profile.

New workspaces use sparse-content digest v2, query metadata v4 and workspace manifest v3. The digest binds the declared axis order, names, titles, regular edges, endpoint policy, flow-bin policy, labels, entries, occupied coordinates, contents and Sumw2. Verification first compares each stored variable-edge axis with the declared layout. The digest does not use ROOT-computed underflow or overflow edge values.

Older metadata v3 workspaces keep their recorded v1 scientific identity. Verification accepts only the runtime v1 encoding or the defined ROOT 6.40 phi-overflow encoding, after the same exact semantic checks. It reports a separate v2 canonical comparison identity but does not replace or re-sign the recorded v1 identity. Collections cannot mix v1 and v2 query identities.

Sparse axes

The following order is part of query.json:

  • sparse_activity: tune, block, a15_eta4, a15_eta1.

  • sparse_triggers: tune, block, a15_eta4, a15_eta1, trigger_pdg, trigger_pt, trigger_eta.

  • sparse_pairs: tune, block, a15_eta4, a15_eta1, trigger_pdg, associate_pdg, sign, trigger_pt, associate_pt, trigger_eta, associate_eta, dphi, deta, origin, category.

  • sparse_kinematics: tune, block, a15_eta4, a15_eta1, pdg, pt, eta, phi.

  • sparse_closure: tune, block, a15_eta4, a15_eta1, trigger_pdg, associate_pdg, trigger_pt, associate_pt, trigger_eta, associate_eta, dphi, category.

Tune and block axes retain source membership. Species axes use the common signed-PDG dictionary. Kinematic axes use the normalized analysis model. Physical inclusive high endpoints occupy the final regular bin. The pT overflow remains distinct.

Exact support rows

The support trees retain these columns. Their scalar C++ types appear in row_schema.hpp.

  • events: event_id, weight, a15_eta1, a15_eta4, process_code, pthat, hard_scale, n_mpi.

  • heavy: event_id, heavy_index, pdg, status, final, selected, pair_eligible, category, nc, ncbar, nb, nbbar, qc, qb, pt, eta, rapidity, phi.

  • triggers: event_id, heavy_index, sector, rejection_mask.

  • pairs: event_id, trigger_heavy_index, associate_heavy_index, sign, dphi, deta, trigger_pt, associate_pt, a15_eta1, a15_eta4, associate_origin, associate_category, weight.

  • origins: event_id, heavy_index, sector, origin, resolution, matched_hard, rejected_hard, depth.

  • closure: event_id, trigger_heavy_index, associate_heavy_index, coefficient, visible, dense_category.

  • constituents: event_id, heavy_index, signed_flavour, constituent_ordinal, origin, resolution, matched_hard, rejected_hard, depth.

  • event_compatibility: event_id, diagnostic_id, cell_id, value.

  • event_ranges: first_id, count, source_id.

  • source_blocks: source_id, assignment_id, block.

  • sources: source_id, tune, logical_id, attempt, events, attempted_events, sumw, sumw2, sumabsw.

  • source_counts: source_id, family_id, rows.

n_mpi, process_code, pthat and hard_scale remain event-level fields. The query omits some analyzed four-vector and ancestry information. Retain analyzed files when those details could support another measurement. Neither format contains individual light-pion momenta for a pion-spectrum-versus-activity measurement.

Collection and merge

A collection index uses schema hadronization_query_collection_v1. Its layout is SHARDED or MERGED. Its state is TEST_ONLY or EXTERNAL_ACCEPTANCE_REQUIRED. The latter requests separate acceptance checks and is not itself an acceptance claim.

The index contains analysis_sha256, layout_sha256, dictionary_body_sha256, campaign and manifest identities, tune ordinals, block count, sources, shards and partitions. File facts contain an absolute path, byte count and SHA-256. Scientific identity excludes physical locators and physical checksums.

Each shard record binds query ROOT, metadata and workspace manifest to its source members and content identity. Duplicate natural or global source identities fail. The expected-source check refuses missing or foreign sources.

A merged collection contains one tune-NN.root file per tune. Each family has one object per original block, named sparse_FAMILY__block_NN. The implementation limits each serialized sparse object to 512 MiB. It never combines all blocks into one oversized object.

Merge receipts bind parent lineage, object counts, cell digests and resulting files. Exhaustive comparison checks the occupied domain, contents and Sumw2. It allows 1e-12 absolute or relative tolerance for summation order. It does not allow missing cells.

The merged index still points to original query workspaces. Reduction uses their exact support rows for event moments, origin diagnostics, boundary handling and natural-heavy accounting. Removal of query shards breaks this collection.

Numerical ROOT

numerics.root uses hadronization_self_contained_typed_root_v4. It contains a typed value graph named nodes, metadata named v4_metadata and direct TTrees. The reader compares each direct table with the typed graph. It rejects missing objects, extra objects and duplicate key cycles.

The graph retains the complete numerical request and result. It includes point keys, physical axes, units, resolved selections, boundaries, source identities, deletion families and provenance. It needs no input collection to interpret stored numbers.

Direct tables use signed or unsigned 64-bit integers, binary64 numbers, booleans and strings. The table schema below uses i, u, d, b and s respectively. The type code follows each field name.

  • bindings: schema:s, request_sha256:s, science_content_sha256:s, collection_kind:s, collection_state:s, collection_index_sha256:s, collection_index_bytes:u, collection_scientific_identity_sha256:s, member_files_sha256:s, source_members_sha256:s, admission_qualification:s, admission_expected_sources_sha256:s, admission_natural_members_sha256:s, campaign_scope:s, campaign_attempts:u, campaign_successful_events:u.

  • points: index:u, semantic_id:s, point_key_sha256:s, role:s, tune:s, quantity:s, component:s, axis:s, bin:i, units:s, center_status:s, center_present:b, center:d, uncertainty_status:s, variance_present:b, variance:d, error_present:b, error:d.

  • event_moments: tune:s, block:u, source_members_sha256:s, scope:s, events:u, sumw:d, sumw2:d, sumabsw:d, event_weight_terms:u, content_sha256:s.

  • support_diagnostics: tune:s, block:u, event_moments_sha256:s, natural_final_hadrons:u, natural_final_weighted_sum:d, charm_constituents:u, charm_constituent_weighted_sum:d, beauty_constituents:u, beauty_constituent_weighted_sum:d, strict_selected_final_hadrons:u, strict_selected_final_weighted_sum:d, pthat_sum:d, hard_scale_sum:d, content_sha256:s.

  • diagnostic_activity: tune:s, block:u, activity_bin:u, events:u.

  • diagnostic_n_mpi: tune:s, block:u, n_mpi:u, events:u.

  • diagnostic_process: tune:s, block:u, process_code:i, events:u.

  • diagnostic_origin: tune:s, block:u, origin:i, category:i, sign:i, rows:u, weighted_sum:d.

  • diagnostic_closure: tune:s, block:u, category:i, visible:b, coefficient:i, rows:u, weighted_sum:d.

  • block_values: point:u, tune:s, block:u, events:u, sumw:d, sumw2:d, sumabsw:d, event_weight_terms:u, event_moments_sha256:s.

  • block_components: point:u, tune:s, block:u, component_id:s, value:d.

  • denominator_parents: point:u, ordinal:u, natural_key:s, status:s, retained_after_algebra:b, pooled_present:b, pooled_value:d, policy_id:s.

  • denominator_deletions: point:u, parent_ordinal:u, block:u, status:s.

  • covariance_points: group_id:s, slot:u, point:u, valid:b, units:s.

  • covariance_factors: group_id:s, slot:u, tune:s, source_family_sha256:s, block:u, finite:b, valid:b, leaf:d, leave_mean:d, centered_factor:d.

  • class_boundaries: tune:s, activity:s, class_id:i, low:i, high:i, events:u, event_weight:d, empty:b, status:s, content_sha256:s.

  • class_boundary_deletions: tune:s, class_id:i, omitted_block:u, source_family_sha256:s, status:s, low_present:b, low:i, high_present:b, high:i, empty:b, weight_present:b, weighted_measure:d, content_sha256:s.

  • collection_members: file_id:s, role:s, shard_present:b, shard_ordinal:u, tune_present:b, tune:s, sha256:s, bytes:u.

  • campaign_tunes: tune:s, sources:u, successful_events:u, submitted_attempts:u, accepted_attempts:u, discarded_attempts:u.

  • campaign_trials: tune:s, scope:s, count_present:b, count:u, status:s, reason_codes:s.

  • campaign_attempt_evidence: outcome:s, evidence_status:s, count:u.

  • selected_tune_exposure: tune:s, successful_events:u.

  • materialization: point:u, status:s, reason_codes:s.

  • g9_science: metadata_json:s, metadata_sha256:s.

The literal g9_science table contains the signed heavy-hadron spectrum selection and normalization. covariance_points maps factor slots to numerical points. covariance_factors retains tune, original block, family digest, deletion value, mean and centered factor.

A numeric branch can contain zero when its corresponding presence flag is false. Always inspect center_present, variance_present, error_present or the relevant field-specific flag. A stored placeholder is not an observed zero.

Status semantics

Field or state Meaning
Materialization PRESENT The requested point belongs to the materialized domain
NOT_MATERIALIZED No result exists for that requested domain element
UNSUPPORTED_QUERY The requested point is outside the supported query contract
Center AVAILABLE A finite center passed its required checks
UNDEFINED The estimator cannot provide a center
UNSTABLE_DENOMINATOR A denominator fails a required stability condition. A pooled center can still exist.
Uncertainty AVAILABLE Finite variance and standard error passed prerequisites
AVAILABLE_ZERO_DISPERSION Valid deletion values have exactly zero dispersion
WITHHELD_UNCERTAINTY An available center can lack a usable uncertainty
EMPTY_CLASS The selected integer interval contains no usable class exposure
INCOMPLETE_BLOCK_COVERAGE Required original source-block exposure is missing
CLASS_BOUNDARY_UNSTABLE Deletion changes a tune-local integer boundary
CLASS_BOUNDARY_UNRESOLVED The threshold or its statistical margin fails resolution
Covariance valid_mask Identifies points with usable joint covariance
PARTIAL_SAMPLE The result does not establish full accepted-campaign closure

Reason codes explain missing or withheld quantities. Finite deletion values can remain stored when covariance validity is false. Consumers must not reinterpret those values as valid uncertainty factors.

Exports and figures

CSV exports include point values, missing states and accounting. Binary64 fields use hexadecimal floating-point strings for exact round trips. Use Python float.fromhex to decode them. Unavailable values use empty fields, not numeric zero.

The literal filenames t1.csv and t1.tex contain natural-heavy accounting. TeX tables preserve integer counts and carry missing states. overleaf-preamble.tex, overleaf-tables.tex and the table check source support document assembly.

Figure directories contain PDFs, canvases.root, drawing-record.tsv.gz and manifest.json. Canvas graph identities retain point semantics and statuses. The drawing record contains coordinates, styles, panel geometry and display decisions. It does not define scientific formulas.

The final package contains numerical/, figures/, the selected config/*.json and a root manifest. Its exact file set excludes computation scratch and the native execution binary. The numerical report still records external execution references.

Lifetimes and retention

Material Lifetime and reason
Raw ROOT and independent inventory Preserve when generator diagnostics or information omitted downstream remain useful
Analyzed ROOT and PASS receipts Preserve four-vectors, ancestry and accepted input authority beyond the query subset
Query workspaces Required for exact support and for current merged-collection reduction
Merged ROOT, index and merge receipts Required for sparse projection and parent verification
External acceptance pins and site records Preserve separately from mutable attempts and adjacent manifests
Numerical ROOT, reports, exports and manifests Preserve with every scientific result
Canvases, PDFs, drawing record and selected configuration Preserve the exact scientific presentation
Build pack and execution receipts Preserve while execution provenance or restart depends on them
Build caches and temporary scratch Reconstructible after successful output verification and retention review
Failed attempts and ambiguous publication stages Resolve failure and publication state before removal

Publication behavior

Analysis publishes files with exclusive hard links after validation. Query and package publication use a no-replace directory operation. Darwin and Linux have separate implementations. The Linux fallback requires owned, private staging and exclusive destination reservation.

The publisher checks path confinement, file types, symlinks, hard links and filesystem boundaries where its contract requires them. It hashes readback after publication. A collision or ambiguous result fails closed. No storage protocol inherits POSIX guarantees without a successful site probe.

Command reference

Command reference

Run commands from a Git checkout. ./hadronization dispatches to the stage parsers below. --help and -h print usage and exit without starting scientific work. Parser defaults are relative to the repository unless stated otherwise.

Options marked required need an explicit value. A boolean flag takes no value. Repeatable options append one value per occurrence. Lists consume one or more values. Every SHA option requires the independent expected digest of the named object.

A read-only command can still import Python modules. Python can create bytecode caches unless PYTHONDONTWRITEBYTECODE=1. A cache-mutating verifier preserves its scientific inputs. The workflow supplies ordered operational examples and prerequisites.

No condor subcommand submits to HTCondor directly. Native condor_submit and condor_submit_dag calls contact the scheduler. Generation contacts its configured scheduler only with --submit and a nonempty eligible plan.

./hadronization doctor

Option coupling and return codes

  • analyze verify accepts a plan or an explicit ROOT/receipt pair. A lone receipt is not a complete shard.

  • query census and collection create require equal-length ordered input and hash lists.

  • Collection admission requires path/hash pairs together. A merged collection requires its merge receipt.

  • Full reduction requires site-work and collector closure. An optional explicit request requires --request-sha.

  • reduce verify and reduce explain accept either ROOT/report/report-hash inputs or package-directory/package-manifest-hash inputs.

  • Figure verification uses the same numerical hashes and presentation configuration as rendering.

  • Package construction must receive the exact configuration used for its figure directory.

Successful commands return zero. Argument-parser errors normally return 2. Scientific and file-contract failures normally return 2 outside the Condor boundary. Query transient operating-system failures can return 75. Condor uses 42 for deterministic failure and 75 for classified transient failure.

Compiled C++ executables are implementation interfaces invoked by these Python commands. They do not share an argparse help interface. Their usage and transport formats reside in their source files. Run the public stage commands to preserve provenance and path checks.

Merged ROOT downloads

python3 data/fetch-merged.py

This helper reads data/merged-download.json. It restores complete ROOT bytes from GitHub release assets without invoking the analysis pipeline.

Option Default Effect
--output DIRECTORY data/work/merged Destination for ROOT files and a .parts cache
--local-parts DIRECTORY Unset Read existing transfer parts instead of contacting GitHub
--verify-only False Check final files without downloading or writing
-h, --help Unset Show help and exit

The default command contacts GitHub and writes local files. It preserves different existing outputs by refusing the operation. See download instructions for storage needs and restart behavior.

Reproduction and recovery

Reproduction and verification

Preserve identities

Record the source commit and tree before execution:

git rev-parse HEAD HEAD^{tree}
git status --short

Keep the campaign, configuration and external input hashes with the run. A file's SHA-256 identifies bytes. A scientific-content digest identifies normalized scientific content. An execution receipt identifies the program and environment. These identities are not interchangeable.

Supply expected hashes from a separate reviewed record. A new hash beside a changed output only identifies its current bytes. It does not restore lost authority.

This Python command computes a file hash without loading the complete file into memory:

python3 - "$INPUT_FILE" <<'PYCODE'
import hashlib
import sys
from pathlib import Path
h = hashlib.sha256()
with Path(sys.argv[1]).open('rb') as stream:
    for chunk in iter(lambda: stream.read(4 * 1024 * 1024), b''):
        h.update(chunk)
print(h.hexdigest())
PYCODE

Set INPUT_FILE to a regular file first. Compare the result with the independent expected digest.

Fresh execution

Use a clean Git checkout with the documented runtime. Set a fresh scratch root and workspace-backed TMPDIR. Run doctor, the required runtime checks and study_contract.py check. Run ./hadronization verify and inspect skipped cases.

Follow the workflow with external inputs from their checksum-bound inventory. Keep original source blocks unchanged. Do not equate new query shards with independent statistical blocks.

For full reduction, preserve accepted site-work and collector-closure records. A collection index alone cannot establish full production closure. A synthetic or partial result must retain its qualification in reports and figures.

A source-only download can support inspection. It cannot supply Git provenance or bulk data. The merged-data downloader retrieves the completed sparse ROOT files. It does not download raw, analyzed or query support rows.

Synthetic example

This example needs ROOT, PyROOT, a C++17 compiler and Git history. It creates synthetic raw inputs and runs analysis, query construction and physical merging. It does not generate a research sample with PYTHIA.

NONZERO_CHAIN_BASE must be an absolute new directory. Its parent must already exist and have no symlink components. Do not select a directory containing other data.

mkdir -p data/work/tmp
export TMPDIR="$PWD/data/work/tmp"
export NONZERO_CHAIN_BASE="$PWD/data/work/nonzero-example"
python3 tests/fixtures/nonzero_chain_v22/build.py
export NONZERO_CHAIN_REPORT="$NONZERO_CHAIN_BASE/oracle.json"
python3 tests/fixtures/nonzero_chain_v22/oracle.py

The builder creates three tune domains with ten original blocks. NONZERO_CHAIN_SOURCES_PER_BLOCK accepts 1 or 2 and defaults to 1. The standalone oracle reads the declared block-object inventory. It independently sums the complete sparse domain and Sumw2, then compares them with the source-query domain.

The resulting collection has TEST_ONLY state. Its merged/index.json and expected-sources.json can exercise reduce run without production site records. Supply independently recorded hashes for these files and config/analysis.json. Do not use --representative to claim complete figure coverage.

The prebuilt query fixture exercises collection and merge contracts. Its version differs from the current numerical input model. Use the builder above for the current model.

Verification boundaries

Command What it checks What it does not establish
analyze verify Shard contract, receipts, rows and provenance bindings Availability of every unselected source
query verify Exact workspace, hashes, support rows and sparse reconstruction Independent custody of a caller-supplied content pin
collection verify Member files, dictionaries, axes and source closure Full site admission without its separate records
merge verify Complete sparse cell domain, contents, Sumw2 and parent lineage Permission to delete original support rows
collection admit Independent expected-source and execution closure A new campaign from incomplete data
reduce verify --mode producer Numerical data plus source and external execution bindings Future availability of external storage
reduce verify --mode portable Self-contained numerical content and exact exports External execution inputs
plot verify-render-cold Reopened canvas semantics, file hashes and source/runtime bindings Human readability or scientific model adequacy
package verify Exact package files, numerical verification and canvas verification External execution revalidation

Copy outputs

Copy the final collaboration package as one directory, including its manifest and selected plot configuration. Preserve the package-manifest SHA-256 separately. Run package verify at the destination with the matching source and a fresh verifier scratch directory.

The numerical package uses relative file locators for its required contents. External execution locators remain recorded but are not opened in portable mode. The final package verifier still checks renderer source hashes and build identity. “Portable” therefore does not mean independent of ROOT, compiler or repository source.

For bulk collection relocation, preserve all file bytes. Update only physical locators in a new collection index and record its new hash. Its scientific identity can remain unchanged. Re-run collection verification and obtain the required independent acceptance records for the new locations.

Retention and Git

Keep bulk raw, analyzed and query ROOT outside ordinary Git. Keep all files required by active collection indexes. Merged sparse ROOT cannot replace query support rows or full analyzed ancestry.

Keep the source commit, configuration, numerical ROOT, exports, canvases, PDFs and compact manifests with a research result. Keep credentials, build packs, scratch, controller state and logs outside tracked collaboration products. See the retention table.

The cleanup command removes reproducible local residue. It does not determine the retention needs of scientific information. Review clean --dry-run before any clean --apply operation.

SHA-256cc2c0593d8b48103560bed7ba46fa7f81a8137bae24994c6ef2316dd9265005d
data/fetch-merged.pydata

Download, verify and concatenate byte parts without repeating the sparse merge.

Reader or caller: Repository users

Inputs

  • data/merged-download.json
  • Public GitHub parts or an explicit local parts directory

Outputs

  • Three exact merged ROOT files
  • Verified cached parts and progress output

Mechanism

The helper checks each part's size and SHA-256 before concatenation. It closes and hashes the reconstructed file before exclusive publication. Restarts reuse complete verified parts. Verify-only performs no download or write.

Failure and scope

Different existing files, symlinked destinations, truncated transfers or unexpected asset URLs fail. It restores bytes without ROOT or a scientific merge.

hadronizationentry

Dispatches stages, reports environment, runs tests and lists or applies cleanup.

Reader or caller: User command line

Inputs

  • Command arguments
  • Study and campaign JSON for doctor
  • PYTHON for test discovery

Outputs

  • Stage exit code and structured command output
  • Optional cache deletion with clean --apply

Mechanism

The entry point dispatches analysis, query, collection, merge, reduction, plotting and package commands to their dedicated parsers. It implements doctor and cleanup locally. The verify command runs unittest discovery. Generation defaults to inventory; submission defaults to continuation.

Failure and scope

A missing dependency can remain optional in doctor. Use the stronger stage-specific runtime check before computation. Cleanup refuses paths that resolve outside the repository.

pipeline/analyze/analyze.cppanalyze

Writes, inspects and verifies typed analyzed rows and embedded contracts.

Reader or caller: Analysis wrapper

Inputs

  • Native analysis specification and raw ROOT sources
  • Contract template and source identities

Outputs

  • Sixteen typed analysis tables and embedded contract
  • Inspection or semantic verification results

Mechanism

The converter expands particle vectors into rows keyed by event and particle. It preserves full retained mother edges, origins and constituents. It constructs structural trigger masks, ordered pairs and signed closure rows. The reopened-file verifier checks schema, natural keys, foreign keys and reconstructed scientific rows.

Failure and scope

Branch, alias, vector, event-ID, origin, pair-population or digest disagreement rejects the shard. Lossless means retained raw information, not the complete PYTHIA record.

pipeline/analyze/run.pyanalyze

Validates campaign inputs, plans shards, builds native tools and manages receipts.

Reader or caller: Analysis CLI and query support

Inputs

  • Campaign, raw manifest and attempt ledger
  • Accepted raw ROOT and expected physical hashes
  • Packing target and optional measured rates

Outputs

  • Immutable analysis plan
  • Analyzed shard ROOT and PASS receipt
  • Build/cache and verification records

Mechanism

The adapter validates campaign domains and source joins. The planner groups complete sources deterministically. Native tools derive from a hashed build identity. A worker hashes input before and after use, verifies reopened output and publishes without replacement. Resume rechecks existing ROOT/receipt pairs.

Failure and scope

Receipt-only output, conflicting bytes, incomplete source coverage, symlinked paths or changed build/configuration fail. Recovery of ROOT-only output needs a valid embedded contract.

pipeline/generate/physics.hppgenerate

Particle valence, status, origin, activity, seed and event-ID rules.

Reader or caller: Producer, raw validator and analyzer

Inputs

  • Particle identities, statuses, mother graphs and kinematics
  • Generated selected-state registry

Outputs

  • Heavy valence, origins and ambiguity states
  • Event IDs, activity predicates and angular transforms

Mechanism

The header decodes conventional meson/baryon valence. It follows signed heavy carriers through expanded mother relations. Uniqueness checks reject conflicting final claims. Separate functions define raw selector predicates, activity, event-ID packing and the auxiliary light-charge grid.

Failure and scope

Unknown or ambiguous lineage remains unresolved. The active downstream no-floor pair selection comes from query/model.py and selection.hpp.

pipeline/generate/producer.cppgenerate

Runs PYTHIA and writes raw event, stability, settings and accounting objects.

Reader or caller: Reserved generation worker

Inputs

  • Effective tune card
  • Reserved tune, job, attempt, seed and event request
  • PYTHIA particle data and runtime

Outputs

  • Raw ROOT event tree
  • Effective settings, stability audit, process summary and job metadata

Mechanism

The producer requests successful PYTHIA events, checks the heavy hard pair and records heavy-particle and ancestry vectors. It disables recognized heavy-hadron decays. It records weights, activity, process code, pTHat, hard scale and MPI count. Final metadata distinguishes successful events, failed trials and completeness.

Failure and scope

Malformed arguments, unsupported identities, initialization failures, invalid hard pairs or failed conservation/origin checks prevent a complete accepted file.

Resolves and checks compiler, ROOT and PYTHIA installations.

Reader or caller: Setup, builders and worker wrappers

Inputs

  • Optional parsed site.conf
  • Current environment and executable discovery
  • ROOT and PYTHIA configuration tools

Outputs

  • Resolved command paths and environment
  • JSON, shell exports or runtime-check result

Mechanism

The resolver combines explicit site paths with executable discovery. It checks declared ROOT versions and the PYTHIA version, prefix, headers, XML data and linker/include flag planes. The same interface serves setup and native builds.

Failure and scope

Duplicate site keys, missing required tools or inconsistent PYTHIA installations fail. A login-shell resolution does not establish execute-node access.

pipeline/generate/submit.pygenerate

Plans, builds, reserves, submits and runs generation attempts.

Reader or caller: Generation CLI

Inputs

  • Campaign, raw manifest and attempt CSV
  • Study and tune cards
  • Runtime and generation intent

Outputs

  • Inventory and deterministic plan
  • Builds, reservations, submit files and attempt outcomes
  • Accepted raw ROOT with validation receipt

Mechanism

The planner joins accepted natural source identities with attempt evidence. It materializes each event count and seed in an effective card. Submission reserves unique attempts before scheduler contact. The worker authenticates inputs, runs the frozen binaries, validates output and publishes by an exclusive hard link.

Failure and scope

Missing accepted bytes are a retrieval problem, not permission to regenerate. Existing reservations, changed binaries, invalid receipts or output collisions stop the attempt.

pipeline/generate/validate_raw.cppgenerate

Checks raw schema, source authority, kinematics, ancestry and metadata.

Reader or caller: Generation worker and analyzer

Inputs

  • Raw ROOT
  • Expected campaign, source, seed, card, executable and version fields

Outputs

  • PASS or diagnostic findings and exit status

Mechanism

The validator checks exact metadata and ROOT schemas. It verifies scalar/vector coherence, identities, kinematics, expanded mother relations, origin uniqueness, heavy content and invariant counters. It compares effective settings with their declared contract.

Failure and scope

A readable ROOT file can still fail semantic validation. The worker must require both successful production and validator PASS.

pipeline/plot/run.pyplot

Checks numerical ROOT, builds presentation plans and verifies figure files and canvases.

Reader or caller: Plot CLI and package verification

Inputs

  • Numerical ROOT with physical and value hashes
  • Presentation JSON
  • Matching renderer runtime

Outputs

  • Drawing plan and native render payload
  • PDFs, canvases.root, drawing record and exact manifest

Mechanism

The wrapper verifies typed results before constructing display panels. It derives labels, cuts, classes and event totals from numerical provenance. It selects display support and styles, compiles the renderer and verifies cold canvas readback. No scientific formula belongs here.

Failure and scope

Mismatched charm recipe, noninclusive paper profile, missing required roles, unrenderable class styles or source/runtime disagreement fails.

pipeline/query/collection.pyquery

Checked collection locator, source admission, sparse iteration and exact support access.

Reader or caller: Collection CLI, merge and reduction

Inputs

  • Query workspaces and independent content pins
  • Expected natural sources and optional site/merge closure records

Outputs

  • Checked sharded or merged collection index
  • Admission and exhaustive merge verification records
  • Sparse partitions and exact support iterators

Mechanism

The reader checks file facts, source domains and common dictionaries. Scientific identity excludes physical locators. Merge verification compares every occupied cell and Sumw2 with the source-query domain. Admission binds independently held expected sources and production closure.

Failure and scope

Duplicate sources, missing files, mixed scientific digest schemas, dictionary drift, invalid merge lineage or false full-campaign claims fail.

pipeline/query/condor.pyquery

Prepares immutable bundles, runs attempts and collects exact accepted closure.

Reader or caller: Condor CLI and generated wrappers

Inputs

  • Accepted acquisition manifest, dictionary and source snapshot
  • Qualified Linux pack and admitted site evidence
  • Externally retained acceptance pins

Outputs

  • Inert and bound bundles
  • Native DAG launch files and immutable attempts
  • Exact collector closure and collection index

Mechanism

Preparation fixes source, input and dictionary domains without submission. Site binding requires actual runtime/storage measurements and four-worker resource limits. Workers use one frozen binary pack, verify inputs and stage closed readback-checked outputs. Collection publishes exact domain closure last.

Failure and scope

The full adapter enforces 323 shards, 3,000 sources and this campaign identity. Deterministic exit 42 aborts; classified transient exit 75 permits at most two retries.

pipeline/query/merge.pyquery

Writes bounded sparse objects by original block in one file per tune.

Reader or caller: Merge CLI

Inputs

  • Verified SHARDED index and its expected SHA-256

Outputs

  • One tune-NN.root per tune
  • Merged index, lineage receipt and verification receipt

Mechanism

The merger scans each sparse family across source shards. It adds matching tune/block cells and records entries independently. It preflights each serialized object, closes the tune file and verifies its objects before directory publication.

Failure and scope

Existing destination, inconsistent geometry, absent tune contribution, oversized sparse object or mismatched cell sum fails. Ambiguous scratch remains available for diagnosis.

pipeline/query/model.pyquery

Normalizes the scientific request and validates profile, registry and compatibility rules.

Reader or caller: Query and reduction

Inputs

  • Analysis JSON and shipped study bytes
  • Construction-time analysis for compatibility

Outputs

  • Validated immutable normalized model
  • Exact primitive routes and coherent D0/D+ recipes

Mechanism

The validator checks exact schemas, axes, activities, signed domains and the K10 estimator policy. It permits compatible profile and percentile changes after construction. It binds inclusive or aligned rectangular selection to the available query axes.

Failure and scope

Unknown keys, off-edge minima, diagonal pT cuts, changed fixed contracts or incompatible source definitions fail. The full released model requires version 2.2.0.

pipeline/query/publication.pyquery

No-replace publication, Linux reservation fallback and readback checks.

Reader or caller: Query, bundle and package writers

Inputs

  • Closed private staging directory
  • Fresh confined destination

Outputs

  • Published directory without replacement

Mechanism

Darwin and Linux use native no-replace operations when available. The Linux fallback reserves a private destination, tracks file identities and checks readback. The code preserves ambiguous stages rather than assuming a failed response means no publication.

Failure and scope

Existing paths, symlinks, unsafe links, crossed filesystem assumptions or concurrent content changes fail closed.

  • Analysis, query layout, campaign dictionary and optional prepared pack

Outputs

  • Prepared executable pack
  • Campaign dictionary census
  • Seven-file immutable query workspace

Mechanism

The wrapper admits source receipts before ROOT open. It separates scientific bindings, execution attestation and physical hashes. Build constructs scratch output, closes and verifies it, then publishes the directory without replacement. A prepared-pack mismatch cannot trigger a hidden rebuild.

Failure and scope

Incomplete census, inconsistent dictionary, input hash conflict, wrong runtime pack or extra/missing workspace files fail.

pipeline/reduce/native_engine.cppreduce

Evaluates requested observables and emits values, deletion factors and primitive receipts.

Reader or caller: Native runner

Inputs

  • Checked additive primitive stream
  • Enumerated point and class request

Outputs

  • Pooled centers and statuses
  • Tune-local deletion leaves and centered factors
  • Block primitives, denominator parents and class boundaries

Mechanism

The evaluator computes each observable from pooled primitives. It recomputes classes and ratios for each block deletion. Tune comparisons vary one tune at a time. It emits the full point domain and independent uncertainty validity.

Failure and scope

Wrong request binding, invalid transport domains, absent denominators or unresolved boundaries produce refusal or explicit point-local missing states.

pipeline/reduce/native_runner.pyreduce

Builds the estimator, maps exact inputs and checks native output streams.

Reader or caller: Public reducer

Inputs

  • Checked source collection
  • Typed complete request and analysis hash

Outputs

  • Compiled native estimator and build receipt
  • Bound primitive, result, denominator and deletion streams

Mechanism

The runner converts exact natural keys to native transport. It compiles the single C++ estimator with recorded flags and runtime. It checks every returned point, block, parent and deletion family against the predeclared request.

Failure and scope

The full research route requires the complete merged three-tune collection. Missing or extra rows, changed hashes and incomplete block coverage fail.

pipeline/reduce/native_v4_result.pyreduce

Assembles native values and factors into the typed result contract.

Reader or caller: Public reducer

Inputs

  • Verified native streams, request, moments and provenance

Outputs

  • Single typed numerical result with recoverable deletion families

Mechanism

The assembler verifies stream order and natural identities. It maps native values into points, denominator records and class boundaries. Covariance groups retain family digests, original block IDs, leaves, finite masks and usable masks.

Failure and scope

Missing provenance, trailing stream rows, duplicate identities or disagreement with the expected domain fails. It does not recalculate a second production estimator.

pipeline/reduce/projection.pyreduce

Typed numerical schemas, natural point keys, request construction and result validation.

Reader or caller: Reducer and renderer reader

Inputs

  • Normalized scientific definitions
  • Source lineage, request and numerical result dictionaries

Outputs

  • Typed request/result contracts
  • Complete point keys, units and semantic parent expectations

Mechanism

The schema enumerates science before execution and validates it after readback. It binds selections, covariance families, class boundaries, source identity and materialization. It preserves numeric values as exact binary64 hexadecimal strings.

Failure and scope

Unknown quantities, wrong point domains, missing parents, invalid statuses or incompatible source receipts fail.

pipeline/reduce/public_v4.pyreduce

Admits complete inputs, runs native reduction and verifies producer or portable packages.

Reader or caller: Reduce CLI

Inputs

  • Merged collection and independent source/site/merge pins
  • Analysis selection and clean source snapshot

Outputs

  • Numerics, exports, accounting and exact numerical manifest
  • Native execution and source/build receipts

Mechanism

The public reducer validates full or synthetic scope, constructs the request, executes the native authority and assembles the typed result. It writes and reopens ROOT, verifies equality and exports tables. Producer and portable verification have separate input requirements.

Failure and scope

Dirty source blocks full production. Missing support, incompatible analysis, incomplete campaign closure or output reuse fails. Portable mode does not certify external execution.

pipeline/reduce/statistics.hppreduce

Pooled ratios, denominator checks, class-boundary resolution and jackknife covariance.

Reader or caller: Native estimator

Inputs

  • Additive block vectors, activity histograms and denominator series

Outputs

  • Pooled estimates, delete-one covariance and standard errors
  • Boundary/denominator screens and diagnostic block summaries

Mechanism

Compensated sums build pooled and deleted samples. The K10 policy uses a 9/10 covariance prefactor and fixed t9 resolution threshold. Existence checks retain semantic denominator parents even when algebra cancels them. Diagnostic block SEM does not select a production method.

Failure and scope

Nonfinite values, incomplete or incompatible block design, unresolved denominator intervals or unstable/unresolved classes withhold affected uncertainty.

No indexed repository dependency.

pipeline/reduce/support_scan.cppreduce

One-pass support scan for event moments, origins, closure and natural-heavy counts.

Reader or caller: Native primitive reader

Inputs

  • Original query support ROOT and source-to-block mapping

Outputs

  • Event moments and activity diagnostics
  • Natural-heavy/constituent counts, origin and closure summaries

Mechanism

The compiled scan joins rows by event and source. It accumulates exact counts and weighted sums for the same original blocks used by sparse projection. Pair counts alone cannot reconstruct these diagnostics.

Failure and scope

Missing trees, mismatched source ownership or invalid exact support values fail.

Assembles and verifies the exact relative numerical and figure file set.

Reader or caller: Package CLI

Inputs

  • Verified numerical and figure manifests
  • Selected plot configuration and current renderer source

Outputs

  • Portable collaboration package with relative locators
  • Exact package verification result

Mechanism

Package assembly checks the figure-to-numerical bindings and selected configuration. It copies the required file set into a fresh destination. Verification checks every file and runs both portable numerical verification and cold canvas verification.

Failure and scope

Extra/missing bytes, changed selected configuration, source mismatch or existing output fails. External execution records remain references in portable mode.

setup.shentry

Resolves the common runtime and exports its environment.

Reader or caller: Bash or zsh

Inputs

  • Shell location
  • PYTHON or python3
  • Optional config/site.conf through the resolver

Outputs

  • Environment exports in the calling shell

Mechanism

The script locates the checkout and asks runtime.py for shell-quoted exports. It evaluates only those resolver exports and removes its temporary shell variables.

Failure and scope

Unsupported shell location or a failed resolver prevents successful setup. The command does not install dependencies.

docs/atlas.htmldocumentation

Self-contained scientific guide, command reference and searchable dependency browser.

Inputs: embedded prose, source inventory, configuration values and dependency records for the stated source revision.

Outputs: browser views, filtered references and a printable document. It performs no scientific reduction.

The document embeds CSS, JavaScript and reference data. It needs no online library. Source links and scientific-data downloads need network access.

The repository README and file reference link to this document. Its Git revision supplies its physical identity. It does not embed a self-referential checksum.

This atlas describes the specified source revision. The linked source, schemas and checks define the implemented behavior.

Repository · Data release · Back to start
